session_read: Weekly deep review, Monday pre-open. Book stable and up: $42,296 total (equity $38,230 + cash $4,067, 9.6% -- back in the normal band), +5.91% P&L, drawdown healed to -5.74%. Six trades since Thursday's close resolved this run's UNCAPTURED backlog via a scoped email search -- INTC entered as a brand-new position, ARM and NBIS re-entered, SNDK/TER/SKHY were added to, and BE was fully stopped out. Sentiment jumped from greed to EXTREME_GREED (80.2) on a VIX-near-52wk-low reading, not a momentum blow-off (NDX RSI a moderate 63.3) -- the desk leans into profit-booking on the names that are both over their own risk cap AND sitting in the one cluster that's over its ceiling (AI Semis/Fabs, +6.91pt over), rather than reacting to the extreme in isolation. Aggregate open risk sits 2.7pt over its 10% cap on eight names, four of them concentrated in Memory/HBM (SNDK, SKHY, MU, DRAM) where Friday's broad SMH+1.96% rally did NOT show up -- confirming those WATCH flags are idiosyncratic (a real SNDK demand-guide miss, an unexplained SKHY drift) and not resolved by the bounce. A rotation pair from CEG->QCOM was retired this run after its downtrend basis reversed and its cluster was found to already be underweight (repeating the exact backwards-logic bug closed last week under a different ticker); a fresh AMD->QCOM pair replaces it, funded and destination both inside the same over-ceiling cluster so the rotation doesn't fight the drift target. Macro backdrop is calm but stretched: hawkish Fed unchanged, no FOMC/CPI/NFP inside two weeks, but SPX near its 52-week high and 10-year yields drifting up +13bp/month argue for some caution on adding fresh AI-capex exposure even though nothing in the book has actually broken.
